_note: Canonical NoöPunk core rules data. PORTED to the tabletop canon in RULEBOOK.md section 4 (2d6 + skill level + attribute modifier against 6/8/10/12/14+) as part of issue #40 Phase C. The previous revision of this file carried a `_superseded_note` recording that it still held the withdrawn 3d6-era engine; that port is now done, so the note is removed and the values below ARE the current canon.
_source_of_truth: RULEBOOK.md. Where this file and the rulebook disagree, the rulebook is authoritative and this file is wrong.

attributes.name: Intelligence
attributes.description: How smart, educated and knowledgeable you are.

attributes.name: Charisma
attributes.description: Your social skills, attractiveness and leadership skills.

attributes.name: Cybernetics
attributes.description: Your cyborg side; how technical you are; your proficiency in cyberspace, programming and cybernetics.

attributes.name: Psyche
attributes.description: Your consciousness, intuition, empathy and psionics. Used in astral projection and for psionics.

skill_check.formula: total = 2d6 + relevant skill level + relevant attribute modifier
_notes: No automatic failure on a natural 2 and no automatic success on a natural 12 (RULEBOOK 4).
No permanent skill-to-attribute binding: the GM selects the attribute that fits the action (RULEBOOK 4).
Helpful or hostile circumstances normally combine into a situational modifier within -2..+2 (RULEBOOK 4).
Skill levels are 0..4 and contribute +0..+4. Unskilled is NOT level 0 (RULEBOOK 4.2, 5.3).

difficulties.6: Relatively simple task that is still beyond ordinary routine
difficulties.8: Significant challenge to a competent professional
difficulties.10: Difficult task expected mainly of a skilled expert
difficulties.14: Extreme task where even a true master will probably fail

_difficulties_notes: RULEBOOK 4 writes the top rung as '14+'. This map pins the five named rungs; a target above 14 is expressed as an explicit difficulty_floor rather than as a sixth rung.

The previous ladder (easiest 3 / easier 6 / easy 9 / normal 12 / hard 15 / impossible 18) is withdrawn and its names are NOT retained as aliases. In particular difficulty 6 keeps its number but changed meaning.
Anything easier than 6 generally should not require a roll.

human_3d6_generation.roll: 3d6 independently for each of the six attributes
human_3d6_generation._note: Attribute generation is unchanged by the 2d6 port (RULEBOOK 5.2, 17.1). This is the RAW 3d6 generation roll and is not the skill-check engine.
human_3d6_generation._range_note: Above +3 is transhuman, below -3 is basically dead. These describe attribute modifiers and define no death/injury/augmentation mechanic (RULEBOOK 5.2).

skill_levels._note: A level-0 skill contributes +0 through level-4 at +4. Unskilled sits outside the numbered levels (RULEBOOK 5.3).

_unskilled_note: RULEBOOK 4.2: an unskilled attempt is either allowed with -1, or blocked when training is required (a blocked attempt rolls no dice).

opposed.formula: 2d6 + relevant skill level + relevant attribute modifier, both sides
opposed._tie_note: RULEBOOK 4.1: if a player character is involved and totals tie, the player character wins. A general tie procedure with no player character involved is deliberately NOT defined; do not invent one.

aiding.helper_rolls: relevant skill + attribute check against the same difficulty

npc_checks._note: RULEBOOK 4.4. Unusually detailed NPCs with attributes and skill levels use the full player-character procedure.
